subject: surgery
title: Digital Rectal Examination and Prostate Assessment

steps.tx: Examination of the prostate with a gloved finger through the rectum is the **digital rectal examination**. It assesses size, surface, consistency and the central groove of the gland. A smooth, rubbery enlargement favours benign growth, while hardness raises concern. The finger feels only the back of the gland, so a normal examination never excludes cancer growing at the front.
steps.say: Digital rectal examination feels prostate size and surface, where smoothness favours benign growth and hardness worries.

vis.caption: Digital rectal examination of the prostate. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: A hard irregular nodule felt in the prostate raises suspicion of **prostate cancer on examination**. Such a finding needs PSA testing and usually biopsy regardless of the blood result. Cancer most often starts in the part of the gland nearest the examining finger.
steps.say: A hard irregular nodule on rectal examination needs biopsy regardless of the PSA result.

steps.tx: Loss of the normal central groove with a firm gland suggests **malignant infiltration**. Benign enlargement preserves the groove and feels elastic. Asymmetry between the two lobes is another warning sign that should never be ignored. A gland over about 30 grams with a rubbery feel and a kept groove can still hide cancer, which is why blood testing pairs with examination.
steps.say: Loss of the central groove with a firm asymmetric gland suggests malignant infiltration rather than benign growth.

steps.tx: A markedly raised blood marker together with a hard gland strengthens the case for **urgent biopsy**. Magnetic resonance imaging before biopsy now targets suspicious areas precisely. This reduces missed cancers and unnecessary sampling of harmless tissue. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging scores lesions 1 to 5, and a score of 4 or 5 usually triggers targeted biopsy.
steps.say: Imaging before biopsy targets suspicious prostate areas precisely and reduces missed cancers.

steps.tx: Bone pain in a man with prostate cancer usually means **skeletal spread**. Dense osteoblastic deposits weaken bone despite looking thick on films. Fractures can occur through involved vertebrae and long bones. Back pain that wakes the patient at night, plus weight loss, should prompt a bone scan even before biopsy results return.
steps.say: Bone pain in prostate cancer usually means skeletal spread with dense but weakened osteoblastic deposits.

vis.caption: Prostate assessment and spread evaluation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Lowering testosterone to control advanced prostate cancer is achieved by **hormone therapy**. It relieves bone pain and slows progression in most men initially. Resistance eventually develops, after which other systemic treatments are added. Leuprorelin injections every three months are the common medical route, and the first dose can briefly flare bone pain.
steps.say: Hormone therapy lowers testosterone, relieves bone pain, and slows advanced prostate cancer initially.

steps.tx: Surgical cure remains an option when cancer is confined, an operation called **radical prostatectomy**. Nerve sparing technique preserves erections when cancer position allows. Continence usually recovers over months with pelvic floor training. Urinary incontinence affects roughly one in five men early after surgery and improves through the first year for most.
steps.say: Radical prostatectomy cures confined cancer, and nerve sparing preserves erections when position allows.

steps.tx: Painful prostate inflammation with fever must not be massaged, a caution in **acute prostatitis**. Rectal examination is gentle because vigorous palpation can push bacteria into the blood. The gland feels hot, swollen and exquisitely tender. Antibiotics must cover coliform bacteria for at least two weeks, and a prostate abscess is suspected if fever persists beyond 48 hours.
steps.say: In acute prostatitis the gland feels hot and tender, and vigorous palpation can push bacteria into blood.

vis.caption: Acute prostatitis: hot tender prostate. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Recording examination findings clearly after every assessment is good **clinical documentation**. Size in grams, surface, consistency and groove status should all be noted. Clear records let later clinicians detect change over time. Examiners expect the groove, consistency and estimated size stated aloud, because vague phrases like prostate enlarged score nothing.
steps.say: Clear documentation of size, surface and groove lets later clinicians detect prostate change over time.
